# Darcy Builds

Darcy Builds is Tom Darcy's manufacturing software studio. Small, useful bits of software for UK manufacturers whose operational processes have outgrown spreadsheets, without replacing their ERP.

Primary URL: https://darcybuilds.co.uk/
Spreadsheet-to-App Sprint: https://darcybuilds.co.uk/spreadsheet-to-app/
Contact: tom@darcybuilds.co.uk

## Customers and approach

UK manufacturers with roughly 20–250 people, existing systems and one operational workflow outside them. Typical buyers are MDs, operations directors and engineering managers. Factory visits to understand the work and build around the team’s process. Every build has a defined problem, output, acceptance criteria, fixed scope and fixed price.

## Offers

- AI Opportunity Sprint for Manufacturers: https://darcybuilds.co.uk/ai-opportunity-sprint/ — typically £1,500–£2,500, starting from £1,500. Half-day or full-day factory visit, staff interviews and workflow review, followed by a short visual report. Aim to identify 5–10 opportunities, assess business value, frequency, data, AI suitability, integration complexity, effort and operational/quality risk, and recommend a first pilot. Priorities are Build now / Investigate / Not worth pursuing. Conventional software may be the better answer. Implementation is scoped and quoted separately. No autonomous machinery control or safety-critical production decisions.

- Spreadsheet-to-App Quick Fix: from £2,000, approximately one week, one tightly scoped workflow.
- Build Sprint: £6,000–£10,000, approximately 2–5 weeks, a typical internal application.
- Larger builds: £10,000+, with scope and schedule agreed together.
- Factory Workflow Audit: £2,500. A day with the team, a process map, problems and waste, rough annual costs, outline solutions, implementation estimates and priorities; a prototype where appropriate. £1,000 credited against a £10k+ build agreed within 60 days.
- Manufacturing Software Partner: reserved improvement capacity after a successful build. £1,000/month for 3 reserved days or £2,000/month for 7 reserved days; minimum three months.

## Example workflows

Production planning, quoting, NCR and rework tracking, job status, inventory, tooling and production reporting. Existing systems can connect through agreed exports, imports or APIs. AI is a tool used where it helps, not the lead offer.

## Case studies

- FactoryPulse: https://darcybuilds.co.uk/case-studies/factorypulse/ — a manufacturing operations tool built by Tom for a client, connecting measures, improvement projects and problem-solving workflows. Genuine screenshots from the product documentation.
- Lightweight Manufacturing ERP: https://darcybuilds.co.uk/case-studies/manufacturing-erp/ — BoM, purchasing, inventory and build status for an approximately 40-person UK manufacturer. Reconstructed screenshots use fictional data.
- Digital Inspection & SPC: https://darcybuilds.co.uk/case-studies/digital-inspection-spc/ — engineering-defined inspections, operator capture and quality analytics. Anonymised project; reconstructed interfaces and fictional measurements.

## Proof

Tom's background spans Rolls-Royce, Atlas Copco, BCG and a venture-backed manufacturing startup. An anonymised project covered a lightweight ERP/MES workflow for a 500+ component automated manufacturing system, connecting BoM, procurement, build status and manufacturing control. No quantified savings or payback claim is published.

## Boundaries

No 24/7 IT support, managed infrastructure, outsourced IT, generic websites, PLC/controls contracting, large transformation programmes, safety-critical software requiring extensive validation or open-ended feature development. Hosting, ownership and support are agreed before each build.

## Ownership and handover

Clients own their data, with access and usable exports agreed. Source code ownership, licensing and access, hosting responsibilities, third-party costs and documentation are agreed before work starts. Hosting accounts sit with the client where practical; managed arrangements include access and transfer terms. Handover covers setup, deployment, data structure, integrations, maintenance and secure account access so another competent developer can take over. An ongoing development retainer is not required to keep using the application; hosting and other service costs remain explicit.
